target_constraint: Must prevent thrombus formation 1-5 years post-implantation
observed_phenomenon: Late stent thrombosis causing myocardial infarction
mechanism: Delayed healing and uncovered struts, along with macrophage-rich neoatherosclerosis and hypersensitivity-associated late thrombosis, are key contributors to late stent thrombosis, indicating that incomplete endothelialization and chronic immune/inflammatory responses drive thrombus formation years after implantation.
intervention: Modify the coronary stent to include a surface coating that actively promotes rapid and complete endothelialization (e.g., endothelial progenitor cell capture antibodies) combined with a sustained-release anti-inflammatory agent (e.g., a corticosteroid or mTOR inhibitor) to suppress macrophage-driven neoatherosclerosis and hypersensitivity reactions, thereby reducing the risk of late thrombosis beyond the 12-month DAPT window.
expected_effect: The stent will achieve complete strut coverage within the first year, suppress chronic local inflammation and neoatherosclerosis, and maintain a quiescent, endothelialized surface, thereby preventing thrombus formation and late stent thrombosis between 1 and 5 years post-implantation without requiring extended DAPT.
falsification_test: In a porcine coronary model, implant the modified stent and compare with a standard DES at 12 and 24 months. Use OCT to quantify strut coverage (uncovered strut percentage) and histology to measure macrophage infiltration and neoatherosclerosis area. The intervention is falsified if the modified stent shows >10% uncovered struts, significant macrophage-rich neoatherosclerosis, or any evidence of thrombus formation at 24 months, or if it fails to show a statistically significant reduction in these endpoints compared to the control DES.
